dependency_closure_observation.summary: Six unpinned top-level requirements resolved to a 35-wheel ARM64 Linux closure dominated by PyTorch and CUDA 13 artifacts.
dependency_closure_observation.version_drift_risk: The requirements are not pinned, so the identical command may resolve differently in a future run even though no drift was observed in this same-day replay.

evidence.offline_causal_test: A distinct fresh client resolved, downloaded, installed, and imported the same dependency closure while DevPI was process-level offline.
evidence.offline_log_semantics: All 35 wheel requests were served locally and no 'reading remote' event occurred.
evidence.snapshot_integrity: The content snapshot verified unchanged after offline replay.

limitations: This is one consumed-development case and one run per condition, so no confidence interval is available.

Direct and cold wrappers returned 124 because the 2400-second timeout fired before the docker run --rm lifecycle returned; verification markers were present, but they are conservatively not counted as in-budget passes.
Whole-machine en0 counters contain unrelated traffic and are supporting observations rather than exact package-byte measurements.
Cold and direct conditions were sequential and therefore include time-of-day network variation.

recommended_batch_policy.frozen_existing_retry: Keep the previously frozen DeepSeek-direct retry cache-disabled.
recommended_batch_policy.initial_state: Create one method-independent seed snapshot from benchmark-visible manifests without using outcomes.
recommended_batch_policy.isolation: Give every compared episode an independent writable runtime copy of the same attested seed snapshot.
recommended_batch_policy.miss_policy: Allow upstream misses so the cache does not close a strong agent's operation space.
recommended_batch_policy.reporting: Report seed construction, hits, misses, upstream bytes, cache bytes, wall-clock, and peak service memory separately from Official Pass.
recommended_batch_policy.rationale: A shared mutable cache across methods creates order effects, while a frozen-offline cache rejects novel packages. Identical isolated online-miss copies preserve fairness and open operations.
